what: What were the town's non-union salary grades and step rates in fiscal 2000?
why: `salary-schedule` and `report-classification-plan` read Schedule A from the 2010 report and FY2011 onward. The 1999 annual town report prints neither: its Textract text (108 of 110 pages with words) was searched for salary schedule, classification plan, salary administration, grade and step, and returned only the Salary Administration Plan named in prose (p28) and in Article 29's merit-increase vote (p94-95: `Article XV of the Town's By-law entitled "Salary Administration Plan of the Town of Lunenburg"`), MCAS grade levels (p43-51), and the DEGREE and STEP columns of the school wage list (p103-108), which name a lane and step per employee but print no rate table (sources/data/report-tables/1999/). — closes: the Personnel By-law Schedule A (salary schedule and classification plan) in force for FY2000, from the Town Clerk or the Personnel Committee.

what: What did each item of Lunenburg's FY2000 capital plan cost?
why: `capital-plans` holds item-by-item costs. The 1999 annual town report prints the FY2000 capital plan only as warrant-article totals with the items named in prose and no amount per item: Article 37 ($4,700, `Capital Expenditure Budget FY2000`), Article 38 ($195,600 asked, VOTED TO BORROW $192,600) and Article 39 ($76,800, capital improvements, funded by five transfers and a borrowing) on p96; the Capital Planning Committee's report (p11-12) names items without costs. The bonds authorized and unissued (p87) list several of the same items with authorised amounts, which is borrowing authority, not the plan. Searched for capital plan, capital planning, capital expenditure, capital improvement across all text pages (sources/data/report-tables/1999/). — closes: the Capital Planning Committee's FY2000 Capital Plan / `Capital Expenditure Budget FY2000` as presented to the May 8, 1999 Annual Town Meeting.

what: How many weighing and measuring devices did the Sealer test in 1999, and what did sealing bring in by device?
why: `report-weights-measures` holds the Sealer's device counts and fees from the 2010 report. The 1999 annual town report prints no Inspector of Weights & Measures report: its text was searched for weights, sealer and sealing and returned only the appointment (p9), the receipts line SEALING FEES $740.00 (p58), the appropriation line Inspector Weights & Measures (p63), the omnibus line WEIGHTS/MEASURES $1,340 (p97) and the inspector's wage (p102) (sources/data/report-tables/1999/). — closes: the Sealer of Weights and Measures' 1999 annual report to the Division of Standards.

what: How much of Lunenburg's debt at 30 June 1999 sat inside the debt limit, and how much outside it?
why: `outstanding-debt` reads this from the five-year outstanding-debt summary the FY2011-FY2025 reports print. The 1999 annual town report prints its bonded indebtedness issue by issue (PDF page 87), a repayment schedule (p86) and long-term debt in the balance sheet's account group (p57), with no summary by purpose and no debt-limit split: its text was searched for debt limit, outstanding debt, long-term and indebtedness and returned only those pages and the index entry `Bonded Indebtedness` (p3). — closes: the Town's FY1999 Statement of Indebtedness as filed with the Division of Local Services.
